observations:
Torah #137 is a two-line aphorism. All bechina-extractable concepts in the Torah belong to one coherent cluster — 'חֵלֶק אֱלֹקִּי מִמַּעַל וְהַקּוֹל הַפְּנִימִי' — which is fully captured by Package 1 in torah_137_packages.json. There are no additional independent bechina families in the text.

The only two bechina relationships extractable from the Torah are:
  (A) 'חֶלְקִי יְיָ' = 'הַחֵלֶק אֱלֹקַּי מִמַּעַל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי' — same divine-portion concept named two ways.
  (B) 'הַחֵלֶק אֱלֹקַּי מִמַּעַל' = 'אוֹמֵר לִי וּמְלַמֵּד אוֹתִי' — the divine portion IS the inner teacher/voice.

Both edges belong to the same single connected component and together form one package. No second bechina domain is present in the text. 'לִשְׁמֹר דְּבָרֶיךָ' (keeping the commandments) is the eitza downstream of the divine-portion cluster — it is the outcome, not an independent bechina domain.

Conclusion: The one package identified — חֵלֶק אֱלֹקִּי מִמַּעַל וְהַקּוֹל הַפְּנִימִי — fully accounts for all bechina-connected concepts in Torah #137. No new independent package is warranted.
